references.Original setting: Four BCI paradigms; within- and cross-subject; compact depthwise/separable CNN; limited-data emphasis
references.IHARQ relation: EEGNet is one P02 neural decoder; IHARQ uses frozen P01 binary left/right task, subject-group split, 160 Hz 8-32 Hz 3 s windows, governed validation/test isolation
references.Comparability: methodological reference only / partial architecture comparison
references.Key use: Motivates compact EEG-specific architecture and source-centered training recipe; not a direct performance benchmark.

references.Original setting: Filter-bank multi-view MI decoder with variance layer; subject-specific/cross-validation settings including OpenBMI/BCIC-IV-2a
references.IHARQ relation: P02 uses author-centered model construction but IHARQ split, binary task, preprocessing, low-label budgets and test isolation differ
references.Key use: Supports use of filter-bank/variance inductive bias; source diagnostics informed Stage12 author-centered horizon.

references.Source: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics 30(5):4134-4147
references.Original setting: Dual temporal/spatial Conformer across MI, seizure and SSVEP under four evaluation settings
references.IHARQ relation: P02 DNN-SEQ resolves to DBConformer with P01-compatibility patch and IHARQ-specific binary subject-group protocol
references.Key use: Context for strong descriptive full-training performance on two IHARQ datasets; headline paper results are not numerically comparable.

references.Original setting: Criss-cross EEG foundation model; masked pretraining; 10 downstream tasks across 12 public datasets
references.IHARQ relation: P02 fine-tunes/uses governed CBraMod branch under P01 binary MI substrate and P02 model-local adaptation
references.Key use: Context for foundation-model branch and the difficulty of transferring generic pretrained representations under constrained task-specific supervision.

references.Original setting: Covariance-matrix classification with Riemannian kernel for MI BCI
references.IHARQ relation: P02 includes Riemannian tangent-space and alignment variants under a common subject-grouped test protocol
references.Key use: Context for competitive classical/Riemannian baselines and covariance geometry.

references.Original setting: 30 pipelines, 36 public datasets; standardized benchmark spanning raw, Riemannian and deep pipelines
references.IHARQ relation: P02 similarly values multi-family, multi-dataset comparison but uses its own frozen P01 split/budget/ablation contract
references.Key use: Supports interpretation that model-family performance is evaluation-regime dependent and reproducible benchmarking matters.

references.Original setting: 10M-parameter pretrained transformer; multi-task EEG pretraining and linear probing
references.IHARQ relation: Not executed in P02; contextualizes contemporary foundation-model direction and challenges of inter-subject/channel heterogeneity
references.Key use: Broader literature positioning only; not an IHARQ comparator.

references.Original setting: Large EEG dataset/toolbox spanning MI and other BCI paradigms
references.IHARQ relation: Source dataset for Lee2019_MI; P01 imposes IHARQ binary labels, preprocessing and subject-group roles
Source dataset for PhysioNetMI; P01 freezes legal left/right MI subset, preprocessing and subject-group split

references.Original setting: 22 EEG channels; four-class MI; competition train/test sessions
references.IHARQ relation: Source family underlying BNCI2014_001; IHARQ uses binary left/right task and own frozen subject-group roles
references.Key use: Dataset provenance and warning against direct comparison to four-class competition scores.

references.Original setting: Few-shot cross-subject MI with task-conditioned prompts, temporal convolution, Transformer and meta-learning on three public datasets
references.IHARQ relation: Context for the continuing difficulty of label-scarce and participant-adaptive MI; P02 does not implement meta-learning or personalization
references.Key use: Recent evidence that low-label/cross-subject adaptation is an active specialized research problem rather than a solved property of generic decoders.

references.Original setting: Standardized multi-task/multi-dataset benchmark of EEG foundation models
references.IHARQ relation: Context for careful evaluation of foundation models such as CBraMod; P02 uses one governed binary MI downstream setting
references.Key use: Supports the need for standardized downstream evaluation rather than assuming foundation-model superiority from pretraining scale.

references.Original setting: MOABB-style evaluation of 1,056 MI decoding configurations across three public left/right datasets; within-participant/session regime
references.IHARQ relation: Recent contextual evidence on participant-specific decoder rankings; IHARQ P02 uses different subject-grouped held-out test roles and therefore is not directly comparable
references.Key use: Supports discussion that average rankings can obscure participant-specific decoder behavior; not used as proof of P02 personalization value.
